Hola Estamos armando un equipo para desarrollar una solución integral de monitorización médica para misiones espaciales de larga duración. El objetivo es crear un ecosistema robusto, inteligente y visualmente impecable que asombre a los jueces y proponga una solución real para cuidar la vida en el espacio.

Para lograrlo, ya contamos con la base de Ingeniería Electrónica y Hardware. Esto garantiza que el proyecto tendrá una infraestructura sólida en la simulación o captura de datos reales.
summary:
What if we could monitor a person's health and environmental conditions in real time, even from miles away? This question inspired us to develop AeroHealth IoT, a project that combines electronics, programming, and the Internet of Things to improve how we monitor important information.
Our prototype uses an ESP32-S3 microcontroller and different sensors to collect data related to vital signs, movement, and environmental conditions. We also developed an interactive web platform that displays this information through graphs, indicators, and alerts.
Our goal is to solve an important challenge: making it easier to monitor multiple parameters from a single platform, without needing to be physically close to the device. To achieve this, we integrated cloud connectivity for remote data access.
Our vision goes beyond Earth. We believe technologies like AeroHealth IoT could contribute to monitoring people in challenging environments, including future space missions.
AeroHealth IoT is more than an electronic prototype. It represents our belief that great innovations can begin with a simple idea and the determination to make it a reality.
details:
What if we could monitor a person's condition in real time, even from thousands of miles away? What if the technology we develop today could one day help us overcome the challenges of space exploration?

These questions inspired us to create AeroHealth IoT, a project born from our curiosity, our passion for engineering, and our determination to turn an idea into something real.

What did we develop, and how does it work?

We developed a smart prototype powered by an ESP32-S3 microcontroller, integrating different sensors to collect information related to vital signs, body movement, and environmental conditions.

But our goal was never just to build a circuit that displays numbers. We wanted to go further.

That's why we developed an interactive web platform that presents measurements through graphs, indicators, and alerts. We also integrated Wi-Fi communication and a cloud server to make remote access to information possible.

Our goal is to bring different technologies together into one connected system.

What benefits does our project offer?

One of the challenges we identified was the difficulty of monitoring different parameters using separate devices.

With AeroHealth IoT, we aim to bring this information together in a single platform, making it easier to access, understand, and analyze.

Our prototype also demonstrates how relatively affordable electronic components can be used to begin developing monitoring systems with opportunities for future improvements.

What impact do we hope to achieve?

Our inspiration doesn't stop on Earth.

Imagine someone working in an extreme environment, where conditions can change unexpectedly and receiving information at the right moment can make a significant difference.

This vision inspired us to explore the challenges faced during space missions.

We understand that our prototype is still in development and would require further improvements and testing before being used in demanding real-world situations. However, we believe it represents a starting point for exploring new possibilities in remote monitoring.

Above all, we want to demonstrate that ideas developed by students can offer fresh perspectives on important challenges.

What tools and technologies did we use?

To develop AeroHealth IoT, we combined different technologies and engineering skills.

For the electronic system, we used an ESP32-S3 microcontroller, along with sensors such as the DHT11, BMP280, MPU6050, MAX30102, and AD8232 to collect different types of measurements.

We programmed the microcontroller using Arduino IDE and C++.

For our web platform, we worked with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, and TypeScript, integrating Wi-Fi connectivity, WebSockets, and cloud services.

Each technology played an important role in bringing us closer to our goal: connecting physical measurements with a digital platform.

What makes AeroHealth IoT creative and innovative?

We believe innovation doesn't always mean inventing something completely new. Sometimes, it means finding a better way to combine existing technologies to solve a problem.

What makes AeroHealth IoT special is how we bring together sensors, electronics, programming, connectivity, and data visualization in one project.

But there is something even more important to us:

We didn't design AeroHealth IoT only by thinking about what it can do today. We also imagined what it could become tomorrow.

Our inspiration from space exploration encouraged us to think beyond a classroom assignment and consider future applications in environments where remote monitoring could be especially valuable.

What factors did our team consider?

Throughout the development process, we considered several important factors, including component costs, energy consumption, ease of use, connectivity, sensor integration, and the possibility of expanding the system in the future.

We also focused on making our website clear and easy to understand, while distinguishing real sensor measurements from simulated data.

The process wasn't always easy. We faced challenges involving electronic connections, programming, and communication between the device and the cloud server.

But every challenge encouraged us to research, find solutions, improve our skills, and work better as a team.

Our Vision

AeroHealth IoT is more than a collection of sensors connected to a microcontroller. It represents our creativity, dedication, and determination to show what we can achieve.

We know there is still much to learn and improve, but we also believe that every great innovation begins with a first step.

Today, we present a prototype developed with our knowledge, effort, and available resources. Tomorrow, ideas like ours could contribute to technologies capable of addressing much greater challenges.

Because we believe the true limit of innovation isn't the distance between Earth and space, but how far we dare to take our ideas.
